document: Working Knowledge settings panel design worksheet
purpose: Editable discussion map of the current custom Rich HUD window. This file is not loaded by the mod.

editing_guide.hierarchy: groups > pages > sections > rows; arrays follow current on-screen order.
editing_guide.current: Reference snapshot of implemented labels, controls and descriptions. Keep this for comparison.
editing_guide.proposed: Enter replacement text or control ideas here. Empty strings mean no proposal yet, not a request to erase text.
editing_guide.details: Draft expanded player help: gameplay effect, tuning direction, a concrete example, and dependencies or limits. These fields are intentionally blank for discussion.
editing_guide.layout: Describe moves, additions, removals, sizing or styling in requested_changes on the relevant group, page, section or row. You can also reorder arrays to propose a new order.
editing_guide.identifiers: Keep setting and action identifiers stable so proposals can be mapped back to code.
editing_guide.notes: Free-form questions, reasoning or feedback; use these fields instead of JSON comments.
editing_guide.scope: Player settings affect the local player. Server settings require administrator access.
editing_guide.numeric_values: accepted_values describes command input, not necessarily slider limits. Percentages display as percent; commands use ratios. Many multiplier sliders cover 0 to 10x with a logarithmic scale and a zero position, even where commands allow 100.

proposed.label: Recent progress duration
proposed.description: Choose how long a schematic stays in your recent progress display.

details.gameplay_effect: Changes display duration only; research and Proficiency gains are unchanged.
details.how_to_adjust: Increase the duration for more reading time, or decrease it to clear the display sooner.
details.example: Use 0 to keep recent history visible until replaced.
details.related_settings_and_limits: The row limit controls how many recent schematics can remain visible.

example.requested_changes: Consider putting the value beside the slider.
example.notes: Example proposal only; not applied to the row below.

window.title: Working Knowledge Settings

entry_points: Rich HUD Terminal > Working Knowledge > Settings launcher
Text HUD API player menu > Working Knowledge > Open settings (when installed; close chat to continue)
current_layout.sizing: Initial and minimum sizes are logical units; window bounds fit the current viewport with 24-unit screen margins and additional scaling when needed.
current_layout.navigation: Plain fixed buttons, transparent background, no sidebar scroll bar
row_layout: Control line: slider on the left, value box on the right
current_layout.game_hud: Temporarily hidden locally; previous HUD state restored on close; progress overlay suppressed while open
current_layout.editing: All edits staged until Apply Changes. Exit/Escape discard unapplied edits. Presets/resets replace prior drafts; other fields update after applying.
current_layout.text_input: Click a value field to activate direct typing without chat. After a 350 ms typing pause, valid values update the local draft and slider. Editing closes on focus loss, discard or loss of edit permission. Apply Changes reads the latest text and commits the draft; normal world saving persists applied settings.

window.notes: There is another popular UI frame works I forgot the name Hud text (the previous hud api) or something, but it might be worth it to also add it's entry point as well. Sizing maybe should be reactive as people use different resolutions and aspect ratios. The current size is a good starting point, but it might be worth it to make the window size reactive to the screen resolution. Though maybe it is already if using world units or something.
window.implementation_notes: Screenshot refinement implemented; pending the next in-game visual review. Footer replaces header close button; plain navigation; staged edits; stacked row controls; local HUD restoration.
